chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when his son Ismail (peace be upon him) died, and he was lowered into his grave. Then he threw himself onto the ground facing the Qiblah, and said: 'This is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Ibrahim.'
Then he said: 'Indeed, a man is lowered into the grave of his father, and he is not lowered into the grave of his son.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on whether a father or son is lowered into the grave during burial?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the specific burial etiquette (*adab al-dafn*) where the deceased is lowered into the grave by a designated person, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s treatment of his son Ibrahim and exemplified by Imam al-Sadiq. It highlights the theological and social distinction in Shia jurisprudence that a father assumes the role of the lowerer for his son, reflecting the father's authority and responsibility, whereas the reverse is not customary. This narration serves as a primary textual evidence for the ritual actions performed during burial, emphasizing continuity with Prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban, from Abndullah Bin Rashid who said,

‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when his<sup>asws</sup> son Ismail died and he was descended into his grave. Then he<sup>asws</sup> threw himself<sup>asws</sup> onto the ground from what faced the Qiblah, then said: ‘This is how Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> dealt with Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man can descend into the grave of his father and he cannot descend into the grave of his son’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Kindiy from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban from ‘Abd Allah ibn Rashid who has said the following: “

I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when Isma’il, his son passed away. The dead body was brought down in the grave. Thereafter he (the Imam) allowed his body to reach the ground on the side of the grave facing the direction of Qiblah. Then he said, ‘This is how the Messenger of Allah did on the death of Ibrahim.’
He then said, ‘A man may enter the grave of his father but a father, should not enter the grave of his sons.’”
